name: Build several different campfire structures
blurb: Different fire lays do different jobs: a teepee for a fast blaze, a log cabin for stability, a lean-to for wind, and a long fire for cooking and warmth through the night.
gear: Graded firewood from pencil-thin to wrist-thick
steps: Learn to grade your fuel first: tinder, then matchstick, pencil, thumb and wrist thicknesses, in separate piles.
Build a teepee: tinder at the centre, kindling leaning inwards. Fast, hot, collapses quickly — best for getting going.
Build a log cabin: square layers of fuel around a teepee core. Stable, long-burning, good coals for cooking.
Build a lean-to: a thick log as a windbreak with kindling angled against it — the wet-and-windy option.
Build a star or long fire for extended burning with minimal tending.
Practise going from cold site to boiling water, and learn to fully extinguish: drown, stir, drown again, and feel with the back of your hand.
tips: Airflow is what separates a fire from a smoke pile. Every lay is really a structure for holding air.
Check the fire regulations and ground conditions before lighting anything, every time.
proof: You build three different lays for three different purposes and can say why you chose each.
